fact_text: Pakistan's power sector has three segments: generation from gas, coal, hydro and nuclear plants plus private IPPs, transmission, and distribution through local DISCOs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's generation segment runs a single-buyer model in which the government is the only purchaser of electricity from power plants.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the single-buyer model the state pays each generating plant a capacity payment to recover its investment and loan repayments, whether or not the plant is dispatched.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The size of a capacity payment depends mainly on the amount invested in the plant, so a costlier plant locks in a larger payment for the life of its contract.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With one buyer, a plant that is not dispatched still needs a guaranteed minimum quantity or a fixed return, which is why the state signs capacity contracts rather than buying per unit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Even a factory built beside a Thar power plant cannot buy electricity directly from that plant, because the single-buyer rule blocks direct sales.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Transmission uses the same capacity-payment model, and much of Pakistan's transmission grid is old, which limits how much cheap new generation can be used.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Apart from K-Electric, almost all distribution companies (DISCOs) in Pakistan are state-owned.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Distribution losses come mainly from electricity theft and unpaid bills, and the cost of those losses is passed on to paying customers through higher per-unit tariffs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IPP investors prefer imported fuel because, under capacity contracts, their fuel supply stays secure even when local supply fails, so fuel-price risk falls on the state.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst suspects plant costs were over-invoiced, and once a higher cost is approved, the resulting capacity payment is locked in for 25-30 years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Nuclear plants have a physical life of 50-60 years, but their bank loans are repaid over about 12 years, which front-loads capacity payments into the first decade.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Load shedding and overcapacity pull in opposite directions: under-investment causes load shedding, while building extra plants raises capacity payments for years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The state asks IPPs to pass their electricity to it at cost, earning no profit on sales, in return for a capacity payment that recovers their investment.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that ending the single-buyer model would make investors forecast which fuel will be cheapest over the next 5-10 years, pushing them to find local gas and coal.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst would keep hydro and nuclear generation under state entities, arguing that this keeps the cheapest sources under government control and lets state supply restrain prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst recommends privatising distribution companies on contract, with the operator paid a share of profit tied to bill recovery, so the state keeps most of the gain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Plants would prefer to supply the DISCO that collects its bills well, so tying generator and distributor economics together aligns both with bill recovery.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thar coal was developed late because the private sector had no incentive to develop it, and a competitive market would bring private capital to local gas and coal.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst sees expensive electricity as a drag on Pakistan's export sector, so power-sector reform is linked to export competitiveness.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Using local gas and coal for power generation would cut Pakistan's energy import bill and support the currency, according to the analyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that combining competitive generation with privatised distribution could halve per-unit electricity prices over several years, though this is a projection, not a forecast he backs with numbers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TWO STEP SOLUTION TO REDUCE ELECTRICITY PRICES IN PAKISTAN FOREVER' (YouTube transcript, undated)
